note: Entity Events is a pure developer API: it re-dispatches the five core entity lifecycle hooks as Symfony events (EntityEventType::INSERT='event.insert', UPDATE='event.update', PRESAVE='event.presave', DELETE='event.delete', PREDELETE='event.predelete'), each carrying a Drupal\entity_events\Event\EntityEvent with getEntity()/getEventType(). You consume it by extending an abstract subscriber base class (EntityEventInsertSubscriber, ...UpdateSubscriber, etc.) and registering it as an event_subscriber service. It has NO config, permissions, routes, plugins or UI. Because there is no per-site config, the medium (introspection) cases are grounded in the enabled module on the live site: the agent must read the actual EntityEventType constants from the running container (the setup guarantees the module is enabled; cleanup leaves it enabled as site baseline). The hard (execution) cases require the agent to build a small custom module with a real event subscriber; verify creates/deletes a probe user_role config entity (entity_events fires hook_entity_insert/delete for config entities too) and checks the subscriber wrote the expected value to Drupal State. Reset/cleanup uninstall the custom module BEFORE deleting its directory to avoid an orphaned enabled module.

evals.prompt: The Drupal contrib module entity_events dispatches an event for each core entity lifecycle hook. What are the five event name strings it dispatches (as defined by its EntityEventType constants)?
evals.expected_output: EntityEventType defines INSERT='event.insert', UPDATE='event.update', PRESAVE='event.presave', DELETE='event.delete', PREDELETE='event.predelete'.

evals.prompt: When entity_events dispatches an event, what object does a subscriber receive and which methods give access to the affected entity and the event type?
evals.expected_output: Subscribers receive a Drupal\entity_events\Event\EntityEvent; call getEntity() for the affected EntityInterface and getEventType() for the event type string.

evals.prompt: Using entity_events, how do I run code whenever any entity is inserted? Which class should my subscriber extend and how is it wired up?
evals.expected_output: Extend Drupal\entity_events\EventSubscriber\EntityEventInsertSubscriber, implement onEntityInsert(EntityEvent $event), and register the class as a service tagged event_subscriber in your module's services.yml.

evals.prompt: By inspecting this running Drupal site's entity_events module, give the exact machine event name that is dispatched after an existing entity is saved (an update).
evals.expected_output: It is 'event.update' (the value of Drupal\entity_events\EntityEventType::UPDATE), discoverable from the installed module on this site.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, entity_events is enabled. By inspecting the running site, give the exact machine event name it dispatches just before an entity is deleted.
evals.expected_output: It is 'event.predelete' (Drupal\entity_events\EntityEventType::PREDELETE), readable from the installed module/container on this site.

evals.prompt: Using the entity_events module's API, create and enable a custom Drupal module named 'entity_events_ins' (under web/modules/custom/entity_events_ins) that contains an event subscriber extending Drupal\entity_events\EventSubscriber\EntityEventInsertSubscriber. When a user ROLE (entity type id 'user_role') is inserted, its onEntityInsert() must store the string "user_role/<id>" (the entity type id, a slash, and the role id) into Drupal State under the key 'entity_events_ins.last'. Ignore other entity types. Enable the module so the subscriber is active on the live site.
evals.expected_output: A module entity_events_ins with entity_events_ins.info.yml (depends on entity_events), a services.yml registering the subscriber (tag event_subscriber), and a subscriber class extending EntityEventInsertSubscriber whose onEntityInsert() does: if $event->getEntity()->getEntityTypeId()==='user_role' then \Drupal::state()->set('entity_events_ins.last', 'user_role/'.$event->getEntity()->id()). Enabled via drush en entity_events_ins -y.

evals.prompt: Using the entity_events module's API, create and enable a custom Drupal module named 'entity_events_del' (under web/modules/custom/entity_events_del) with an event subscriber extending Drupal\entity_events\EventSubscriber\EntityEventDeleteSubscriber. When a user ROLE (entity type id 'user_role') is deleted, its onEntityDelete() must store the string "user_role/<id>" into Drupal State under the key 'entity_events_del.last'. Ignore other entity types. Enable the module on the live site.
evals.expected_output: A module entity_events_del (depends on entity_events) with a services.yml registering an event_subscriber, and a subscriber extending EntityEventDeleteSubscriber whose onEntityDelete() does: if entity type id === 'user_role' then \Drupal::state()->set('entity_events_del.last', 'user_role/'.$event->getEntity()->id()). Enabled via drush en entity_events_del -y.
